articles.title: ‘You can’t make this stuff up’: why we remain fascinated by Elizabeth Holmes
articles.summary: The entrepreneur turned fraudster is the subject of an Oscar-tipped new documentary that takes an unusual look at her strange legacy. David Agus’s first encounter with Elizabeth Holmes at a health conference came as a shock. The Holmes he met in the green room was personable and pleasant.
body: “The accent changed: this deep voice, very serious,” Agus, a medical oncologist, recalls by phone from Los Angeles. “It was as if I had met a person and then interviewed a separate person. That transition from the green room to the stage – I had never experienced something like that before.”

Holmes is not like you or me. She was still a teenager when she founded Theranos, touting technology capable of performing medical tests using only a few drops of blood. She cultivated a distinctive persona: blond hair, an unblinking gaze, a husky voice and a black turtleneck worn in homage to Apple co-founder Steve Jobs.

Holmes mesmerised investors and board members including Rupert Murdoch, Larry Ellison, Carlos Slim and former secretaries of state Henry Kissinger and George Shultz. She became America’s youngest self-made female billionaire. But it was all an illusion, a confidence trick built on a scam. Holmes’s shining career ended in disgrace and imprisonment.
points: The entrepreneur turned fraudster is the subject of an Oscar-tipped new documentary that takes an unusual look at her strange legacy.
David Agus’s first encounter with Elizabeth Holmes at a health conference came as a shock.
The Holmes he met in the green room was personable and pleasant.
“The accent changed: this deep voice, very serious,” Agus, a medical oncologist, recalls by phone from Los Angeles.

articles.title: Mahershala Ali Cries Recalling ‘Moonlight’ Scene, Keeps Quiet on ‘Spider-Verse’ at London Talk: ‘I’ve Got to Be Careful’
articles.summary: Mahershala Ali broke down in tears on stage at the BFI London Film Festival on Saturday as he recalled the young boy at the heart of “Moonlight.” The Barry Jenkins drama won him one of his two Oscars and recently marked its 10th anniversary.
body: “Any time people put flesh on the bones of those who haven’t been seen or had their moment, I think it’s important,” he said once he had composed himself. “I think ‘Moonlight’ was able to make those characters people… make it personal.”

To play Juan, Ali drew on a man he had known all his life, an uncle-like figure he had grown up playing basketball with who also worked as a substitute teacher. The man was arrested and sent to prison while Ali was in college, which left the actor stunned.
“I thought of him a lot in the making of the film because of how human everyone was in my environment and in my upbringing,” Ali said.

He was candid about the backlash that followed “Green Book,” in which he played pianist Don Shirley opposite Viggo Mortensen. It was his first role of that magnitude, and the backlash included the controversy over what Shirley’s family had and hadn’t sanctioned.

The Barry Jenkins drama won him one of his two Oscars and recently marked its 10th anniversary.
“Any time people put flesh on the bones of those who haven’t been seen or had their moment, I think it’s important,” he said once he had composed himself.

articles.title: ‘The Angry Birds Movie 3’ Unpacked by VFX Supervisor, Including Red’s Redesign and Character-Effects Automation: ’He’s Similar by Choice’
articles.summary: The red-feathered hero of “The Angry Birds Movie 3” looks reassuringly familiar, but DNEG Animation had to rebuild much of him to bring the franchise back to theaters.
body: The technical handover was anything but straightforward. In fact, proprietary grooming, rigging and surfacing tools used on the predecessors could not simply be transferred to DNEG’s pipeline. “We had to start from this. A plucked chicken version of Red,” Harboun joked, displaying a bare digital model. Even its underlying geometry needed reworking before the team could reconstruct its feathers.

The result deliberately avoided a radical makeover. Red’s plumage became slightly softer, while his eyes and beak gained firmer, more toy-like surfaces. “Once an IP becomes popular, it kind of belongs to the fans, and we have to respect that,” Harboun said. “We can’t just add our own spin just to give our mark.”

The studio scrutinized the earlier movies frame by frame. “We analyzed the past movies to find the unwritten rules of animation,” he explained. Animators cataloged the angles of Red’s beak, the geometry of his narrowed eyes and the boundaries beyond which a stretched expression stopped feeling like Red. The lessons became a style guide and a reusable library of facial expressions.
points: The red-feathered hero of “The Angry Birds Movie 3” looks reassuringly familiar, but DNEG Animation had to rebuild much of him to bring the franchise back to theaters.

articles.title: Joel Coen Talks Studio Consolidation – ‘Competition Is What Produces Opportunities for Different Kinds of Movies’ – and Teases Reunion Film With Brother Ethan
articles.summary: The Coen brothers could be heading back to their hometown in Minneapolis for a reunion movie eight years after their last joint film, “The Ballad of Buster Scruggs.” While at Lyon’s Lumière Film Festival, where they received a career tribute, Joel and Ethan Coen revealed they have several projects…
body: “Yes, there are a couple of other stories that we’ve thought about that would take place in Minneapolis, which is where we come from. So we’ll see if they haven’t sort of germinated to the point where we would go, you know, that’s what we’re going to do next, or we’re even going to definitely do,” said Joel Coen.

Joel was responding to a challenge from Oscar-winning actor Frances McDormand, his wife of 42 years, who had playfully urged them on stage at the Lumiere ceremony to complete the unofficial trilogy that began with “Fargo” and “A Serious Man.” “I think Fran wants to see it. We’ll see if we can accommodate her,” Joel joked.

Since Netflix’s “The Ballad of Buster Scruggs,” Joel went on to direct “The Tragedy of Macbeth,” starring McDormand and Denzel Washington, while Ethan made “Drive-Away Dolls” and “Honey Don’t!,” both co-written with his wife and longtime collaborator Tricia Cooke.

But the brothers said they have continued writing together and have several unproduced scripts. “We’ve written a lot of scripts that we’ve never made,” Ethan said. Joel then joked that “one of which we could not find on the computer.”

articles.title: Pathé Unveils Sofia Coppola’s ‘Marie Antoinette’ 4K Restoration as Sophie and Jérôme Seydoux Are Feted in Lyon
articles.summary: Sofia Coppola’s cult classic “Marie Antoinette” and three works by Louis Daquin, a champion of the Communist Resistance during the German occupation, are among the latest restored works from French studio Pathé.
body: The studio is currently marking the 20th anniversary of Coppola’s film with the release of a newly restored 4K version on Nov. 25.
The film, which stars Kirsten Dunst and Jason Schwartzman, comes just in time for the recently announced special exhibition at the Chateau de Versailles dedicated to the movie.

The 4K restoration is being supervised by Sony Pictures Entertainment in collaboration with American Zoetrope. It follows the late Eleanor Coppola’s new documentary on her daughter’s film, “ Making Marie Antoinette.”

Pathé is also celebrating the work of Daquin, described by the Lumière Festival as “a unique figure in French cinema, for whom filmmaking and political commitment were one and the same. A member of the Resistance, a staunch communist and union activist heavily involved in defending film industry workers, he considered his craft to be an extension of his convictions.”

articles.title: Mahershala Ali Put His Two Oscars Into a Cabinet: “I Felt a Sense of Accomplishment, Not Fulfillment”
articles.summary: In London, the star also discussed playing people who "haven’t been seen," nearly going crazy on 'True Detective,' police brutality and how 'Green Book' made him feel like a "golden boy," followed by vitriol.
body: BAFTA and two-time Oscar winner Mahershala Ali shared insights into his work, career and new existential crime thriller, Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, at a crowded London cinema on Saturday.
He spoke during a Screen Talk session as part of the 70th edition of the BFI London Film Festival (LFF), which wraps up on Sunday.

How did he feel about the two Oscar wins? “I felt a sense of accomplishment, which is not fulfillment,” the star shared. “Those are different experiences. … Even gratitude is different from accomplishment, which is different from fulfillment. I feel I’m closer to that space now of feeling fulfilled on some level in terms of the work.”

In that context, he pointed out that his newest role is only his second lead role after Swan Song. Indeed, in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, Ali stars as Latif, a devout Muslim and contract killer who travels across Houston in an effort to protect his three children following the death of his wife. He faces dangerous obstacles, including John Cho’s Haun Yoon, an Army veteran and militant church leader who is determined to destroy what he deems great evils.

articles.title: Crystal Lake Episode 6 Revisits A Key Location From The Friday The 13th Movies
articles.summary: Crystal Lake is full of little callbacks and Easter eggs to the Friday the 13th saga, and one key location seems to get attention in Episode 6.
body: After a long wait, "Crystal Lake" Season 1 is finally here. The Peacock series didn't have an easy road to release. The "Friday the 13th" prequel lost showrunner Bryan Fuller in May 2024, with Brad Caleb Kane ("It: Welcome to Derry") eventually taking over. Kane's version pulls back the curtain on the Voorhees family, filling in a lot of gaps in Jason's past, as well as his mother Pamela's. That includes adding some context to a key location from the movies.

The series follows single mother Pam Voorhees (Linda Cardellini) who is grieving after her young son Jason drowned at Camp Crystal Lake. In the aftermath of the incident, strangers arrive at Pam's door digging into her past, setting off a disturbing chain of events. The show takes place mostly in 1972, eight years before the events of the original 1980 slasher classic, which saw Pam killing would-be camp counselors as a means of vengeance on behalf of her son, Jason.

articles.title: Actress Selma Blair says she 'did not intend to harm anyone' in plane altercation
articles.summary: A publicist for the actress said the incident stemmed from a "medical emergency" and said she has a neurological disorder that can cause out-of-control responses.
body: US actress Selma Blair has spoken out after being accused of assaulting multiple people on a flight to New York.

A publicist for the Legally Blonde star said she "did not intend to harm anyone" and that there was "much more to this story". Blair "experienced a medical emergency on the flight" and is still fighting ​multiple sclerosis (MS), a statement read.
Blair's publicist said that the 54-year-old had a neurological disorder that "bears directly on how a medical episode presents to people who do not know her".
The star pleaded not guilty to charges that she assaulted an officer and a nurse after being removed from the flight. She was also accused of assaulting two flight attendants on board.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077's Movie Adaptation Comes With One Controversial Twist
articles.summary: The Cyberpunk 2077 movie is going to take a controversial approach to telling its story, and it's sure to have video game fans arguing on message boards.
body: "At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game. We want to tell a story in the world of 'Cyberpunk,' but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story."

With respect to all the chooms who were gearing up for Keanu Reeves to reprise his role as the punk-rocker Johnny Silverhand and dreaming about all their fan-casts over who could play main protagonist V, allow us to throw some cold water real quick. Whatever form this movie based on "Cyperpunk 2077" ultimately takes, we now know for sure that it won't be a direct copy-and-paste job of the story from the game... and we couldn't be more relieved to hear it.

In other words, perhaps taking the same approach as Zach Cregger's "Resident Evil" is the only way to go. Like Raccoon City, Night City and the surrounding area lend themselves to endless amounts of storytelling possibilities. There's zero reason to give us more of the same ol' stuff when we could get something new and original instead.
points: The Cyberpunk 2077 movie is going to take a controversial approach to telling its story, and it's sure to have video game fans arguing on message boards.
"At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game.

articles.title: Masterplan review – Stanley Tucci is wasted in Amazon’s smooth-brained heist caper
articles.summary: A ‘family’ of criminals attempt to steal the Mona Lisa from the Louvre in pulpy and forgettable thriller. In the last half-decade Stanley Tucci has been a source of near-inexhaustible on- screen delight, whether making friends with nonnas in his delightful cooking shows or smartly judged supporting…
body: There’s a good bit of pulpy fun to have here, with double, triple and quadruple crossing, silly spy gadgetry which has been updated to include retina scan cloning and something called “VR intrusion”. As British criminal mastermind Roger, Tucci is game to send up aristo archetypes, even if his character often veers into parody. “I’m English,” his character says at one point. “‘Not bad’ is what I say when I orgasm.”

Just as you settle in for an evening of will-they-won’t-they hijinks, the film pulls a bait and switch. It turns out that the pair have been set up by Roger (Tucci), a veteran thief himself who has the “job of a lifetime” for them: a decade-in-the-making plan to make off with the Mona Lisa in a complicated scheme that involves drones, trickery, truffle-related espionage and a long-forgotten tunnel that conveniently exists under the Louvre. Also: they are in fact brother and sister, the result of an energetic mid-90s for Roger when he seduced their respective mothers.

articles.title: The Star Trek And Doctor Who Crossover Miniseries Was Killed By One Ridiculous Thing
articles.summary: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds and Doctor Who very nearly crossed over, only for corporate interests to muck things up in the worst way.
body: Why didn't "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" and "Doctor Who" cross over? The short of it: corporate bickering.

Yes, it's been well documented by now that "Strange New Worlds" and "Doctor Who" nearly collided at one point. Indeed, "Strange New Worlds" co-showrunner Akiva Goldsman has admitted that he and "Doctor Who" writer Russell T. Davies tried to hash out what this crossover would look like. One of the fun ideas they had was to make Pelia (Carol Kane), the USS Enterprise's chief engineer on "Strange New Worlds," one of the Doctor's previous time-traveling companions. This was even teased in the "Strange New Worlds" episode "New Life and New Civilizations," where Pelia noted, "Remind me to tell you about the time I spent with a time-traveling doctor I once knew."

"They were dying to do it. Actually, they've started talking about it. Akiva Goldsman mentioned it in an interview the other day. We were dying to do it. It reached the point where me and Steven Moffat had tickets booked to go to L.A. to go to the writers' room to try to work out how to do it."
